policy_text: This policy covers physical damage to the insured vehicle resulting from a collision with another vehicle or object, regardless of fault, subject to the applicable deductible.
Damage arising from a single-vehicle collision, including striking a stationary object or guardrail, is covered under this policy.
Multi-vehicle collisions involving two or more insured or third-party vehicles are covered up to the policy limit.
This policy does NOT cover collision damage if the insured vehicle was being driven by an unlicensed or unauthorized driver at the time of the incident.
In the event of a side, front, or rear collision, the insured must report the specific point of impact accurately in the claim narrative for the claim to be processed.
This policy covers loss of the insured vehicle due to theft, provided a police report is filed within 24 hours of discovering the theft.
Vehicle theft claims are NOT covered if the insured vehicle was left unlocked or with keys inside at the time of the theft.
A valid police report is a mandatory condition for any vehicle theft claim; claims submitted without one will be denied.
Property damage to third-party vehicles or structures caused by the insured vehicle is covered up to the property damage liability limit stated in the policy schedule.
This policy does NOT cover property damage caused intentionally by the insured or any household member.
Claims involving reported property damage must include photographic or documentary evidence of the damage at the time of filing.
Medical expenses for bodily injury sustained by the insured or passengers as a result of a covered collision are reimbursed up to the injury claim limit.
Bodily injury claims are NOT covered if the injury resulted from the insured operating the vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Injury claims exceeding the minor-injury threshold require supporting medical documentation from a licensed practitioner.
If the cost of repairing the insured vehicle exceeds its actual cash value, the claim is settled as a total loss at the vehicle's pre-incident market value.
Total loss settlements require an independent damage assessment confirming that repair costs exceed the total loss threshold.
Trivial or minor damage not affecting the vehicle's structural integrity or safe operation is covered subject to a reduced payout under the minor-damage clause.

This policy does NOT cover any incident that occurs while the insured is engaged in high-risk recreational activities, including but not limited to skydiving, bungee jumping, or base jumping, at the time of loss.
Claims arising directly from participation in extreme sports such as paintball or motor racing on a closed circuit are excluded from coverage.
The insured must contact the appropriate authorities (police, fire, or ambulance) immediately following any incident involving injury, theft, or significant property damage.
All claims must be reported to the insurer within 30 days of the incident date; late reporting may result in denial of the claim.
If witnesses were present at the scene of the incident, their contact details must be provided as part of the claim documentation.
The insured is responsible for paying the policy deductible before any collision or comprehensive claim payout is issued.
Higher deductible plans result in a lower annual premium, while lower deductible plans increase the annual premium payable by the insured.
Only vehicles registered under the insured's name or an immediate family member's name at the time of policy binding are eligible for coverage under this policy.
This policy does NOT cover vehicles used for commercial purposes, including ride-sharing or delivery services, unless a commercial rider is explicitly added.
Where an umbrella limit is specified in the policy schedule, it provides additional liability coverage beyond the standard policy limits for major incidents.
This policy does NOT cover any claim found to involve material misrepresentation, staged incidents, or falsified damage estimates by the insured.
The insurer reserves the right to investigate any claim showing inconsistencies between the reported incident details and the supporting evidence before approving payout.
Damage to the insured vehicle while legally parked and unattended, caused by a third party or external event, is covered under comprehensive coverage.
